name: libva
recipe_basis: The archive is committed for provenance of the generated bindings only; no C sources are compiled from it. build.rs links the runtime libva shared libraries already present on the Linux system (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libva.so and libva-drm.so).
linkage: Dynamic link against the system installation of libva/libva-drm at runtime on Linux; the archive is not extracted during the Rust build.
build_prerequisites: Nothing extra for the Rust build: the VA-API bindings are pre-generated and committed in src/vaapi/bindings.rs, so bindgen, libclang and the headers are only needed when regenerating bindings (tools/gen_vaapi_bindings.ps1). Running fastcord on Linux needs the distribution libva2 and libva-drm2 packages; the drm device discovery uses /dev/dri/renderD*.
rust_binding_decision: The upstream libva-sys/egovva crates run bindgen, pkg-config and Meson during build and cannot be pinned reproducibly offline. Bindings were instead generated once offline from the pinned archive with bindgen 0.73.2 (tools/vaapi_bindings_wrapper.h + tools/gen_vaapi_bindings.ps1, codec families unused by fastcord blocklisted) and committed. The bound surface is the VA-API 1.24 public ABI: device enumeration, config/context/surface/buffer management, H.264 encode and decode structures and the DRM display lookup; these layouts are part of the stable libva runtime ABI offered by the corresponding 2.24.x packages, which build.rs requires at link time.
license_file: COPYING inside the archive; reproduced in docs/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
